study type: Mixed-methods study, including a case-control survey, semi-structured individual in-depth interviews, a focus group discussion, and unstructured direct observations.
exposure: care-related risk factors for complete wound dehiscence
characteristics of interest related to wound dehiscence
cesarean deliveries performed by junior residents
ineffective structure and process of clinical skill transfer
negative experience of care from patients and their families
outcome: complete wound dehiscence after cesarean section
cohort: The study included 524 women (131 cases of complete wound dehiscence and 393 controls who had cesarean deliveries) and care providers from Muhimbili National Hospital in Dar es Salaam.
finding: Complete wound dehiscence after cesarean section was highly associated with suboptimal surgical technique, ineffective clinical skill transfer, negative patient experiences, and was more likely in cesarean deliveries performed by junior residents (OR 1.8, 95% CI 1.7-5.4).
cross-section timing: The case-control data covered cesarean deliveries between January 2015 and December 2020, while qualitative data was collected between July 2020 and December 2020.
